## Same crash confirmed — additional evidence (Windows 11, v1.14.18, Bun v1.3.11)

Experiencing the exact same crash with identical symptoms. Adding my evidence to help with diagnosis.

### Environment
- **OpenCode Desktop**: v1.14.18
- **Bun**: v1.3.11 (bundled sidecar `opencode-cli.exe`)
- **OS**: Windows 11 Home 26200
- **RAM**: 32 GB
- **CPU**: AMD Ryzen 9

### Observed behavior

The sidecar crashes with the same `panic: integer does not fit in destination type` after memory grows to ~15-25 GB RSS. Multiple independent triggers observed:

**Trigger 1: Startup — no user action needed**
Simply launching OpenCode Desktop causes Bun memory to spike from ~600 MB to 15+ GB within 60 seconds, then crash. This reproduces consistently.

**Trigger 2: `/compact` command**
Running `/compact` on a session with 264 messages (2.0 MB content) causes memory to grow from 635 MB to 15+ GB in ~86 seconds, then crash with:
```
RSS: 11.84GB | Peak: 19.81GB | Commit: 28.04GB | Faults: 16,540,592
panic(thread 48480): integer does not fit in destination type
Sidecar terminated code=Some(3) signal=None
```

Crash report: `https://bun.report/1.3.11/ea1af24e28mhGuhooC6gngQs347Myw16Jg3rgNCYKERNEL32.DLLut0LCSntdll.dll4/hjBA0eNoFwcENACAMAsBVWM1ENHyosXzc3js53LyYx`

**Trigger 3: Stale git index.lock in snapshot directory**
A zero-byte stale `index.lock` in `~/.local/share/opencode/snapshot/<hash>/` caused the snapshot service to enter a retry storm, generating 845 index.lock errors and spawning 136 orphaned git child processes. This drove opencode-cli.exe to 11,203 handles / 5.3 GB working set before crash (normal: ~335 handles / 635 MB).

### Additional data
- **OpenCode SQLite DB**: 89 sessions, 6,112 messages, 151.2 MB total content
- **Largest session**: 79.4 MB (617 messages) — likely contributing to startup memory pressure
- **Desktop log**: `$LOCALAPPDATA/ai.opencode.desktop/logs/opencode-desktop_2026-04-20_17-39-35.log` contains the full crash trace
- **v1.14.19 tested**: Still crashes with the same panic — Bun v1.3.11 likely still bundled

### Workaround attempted
- Deleting stale `index.lock` files and restarting fixed Trigger 3
- No workaround found for Triggers 1 and 2 — OpenCode is currently unusable on this machine
- Rolling back to v1.4.5 to test if an older Bun runtime avoids the crash

**Root cause aligns with Bun PR #29327** — the `ssize_t` → `int` truncation in `uv_fs_read` on Windows.

Hey Everyone! So last week the [Kiro T&C/FAQs](https://kiro.dev/faq/#with-which-tools-can-i-use-my-kiro-subscription) were updated to introduce the following:

    Kiro subscriptions can be used with Kiro IDE, Kiro CLI, ACP compatible IDEs, and automation in software development (ex: reviews during CI/CD). Use with OpenClaw and similar tools that leverage third-party harnesses is prohibited.

This makes the kiro-ai-provider implementation go directly against them, so I've created a new ai-sdk compatible [kiro-acp-ai-provider](https://www.npmjs.com/package/kiro-acp-ai-provider) package that leverages Kiro ACP (via kiro-cli) and updated the PR to use it.

The old implementation is still accessible through branch [feat/kiro-provider-alt](https://github.com/NachoFLizaur/opencode/tree/feat/kiro-provider-alt) in my fork for reference, but it's not compliant with the current T&C and therefore it cannot be added to opencode.

Most of the functionality is kept with the new provider, except:
- Requires kiro-cli to be installed.
- Auth handled through kiro-cli login (the WebUI handles it as a standard OAuth flow, but the kiro login page will open automatically).
- No thinking mode (not exposed through ACP).
- No subscription quota display (not exposed through ACP).

Token count and context window usage are maintained. The cost now shows the current session's credit usage instead.

I've submitted a fix for this issue in PR #23592.

**Root Cause**: The Zod schemas in `openai-compatible-chat-language-model.ts` require `id: z.string()` for tool call IDs, rejecting numeric values.

**Fix**: Modified the schemas to accept both string and numeric IDs using `z.union([z.string(), z.number().transform((v) => String(v))])`. Numeric IDs are automatically coerced to strings, making the fix backward-compatible with all existing providers.

**Changes**:
- Modified `OpenAICompatibleChatResponseSchema` tool_calls.id schema
- Modified streaming chunk schema tool_calls.id similarly  
- Updated error message for missing ID
- Added test case for numeric tool call IDs

Closing as duplicate of #22612 which already addresses this issue and has been confirmed working. The approaches are similar - both coerce numeric IDs to strings in the Zod schemas.

Update: There's already an open PR #22612 that fixes this issue. It uses a similar approach with `z.preprocess` to coerce numeric IDs to strings. I've closed my duplicate PR #23592.

Please see #22612 for the fix.

I think the main issue here is that Kimi for Coding does not appear to select the real backend model purely from the `model` field.

From what people have tested so far, the effective model seems to depend more on the auth flow than on whether OpenCode sends `kimi-k2.5` or `kimi-k2.6-code-preview`:

- API key path -> appears to stay on the K2.5 route
- official kimi-cli OAuth path -> appears to reach the K2.6 / `k2.6-code-preview` route

So this PR is still useful as client-side metadata / compatibility support, but by itself it probably does not guarantee “real K2.6 access” for users on the normal API-key path.
